- [x] Title: inrange() with a missing bound selected no rows, in both modes
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py at a2c7502: `_stata_if_to_pandas` (10754; its `_inrange' at 10804-10810)
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 with StataNow 19.5 by WP-24's function audit.  Stata reads a missing bound of inrange() -- `.' or `.a' to `.z' -- as no bound: inrange(x, ., 3) is x <= 3, inrange(x, 1, .) is x >= 1 and inrange(x, ., .) every non-missing x, and a missing x is never in range.  dash wrote ((x >= a) & (x <= b)) whatever the bounds, and the rewrite of Stata's missing idioms that follows it read `x >= .' as "x is missing": inrange(x, ., 3) and inrange(x, ., .) selected no row, and a bound of .a to .z was left as invalid syntax, so the qualifier was skipped and every row drawn.  Every graph, layer and KPI `if' was affected, saved and served.
  - Suggested fix: Leave out the comparison with a missing bound, and write (x == x) when both are missing.
  - Resolution: Fixed as suggested.  A bound that is a variable holding a missing value in some rows is still compared as NaN, which excludes those rows where Stata would not bound them; dash.ado exports what the qualifier names, so that case is reachable, and is not covered here.  Certified by test/test_function_audit.py::TestQualifierFunctionsSelectStatasRows (KPI cards in both modes held to Stata's own rows), which fails 8 of its cases with the old translation.

Whether the browser draws those lines correctly was not checked.

Not fixed: it stays open because WP-24 changed tests only, and whether the lines are drawn wrong has not been measured.  **Fixed 24sep2026 (WP-27).** `map_line' applies a layer's view to the rows in the caller's order before sorting by x and attaches no filter to the Line, as `map_area' does. - [x] Title: A qualifier that abbreviates a variable is skipped by the renderer, and every row is drawn
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py at a2c7502: `_stata_if_to_pandas` and `_dash_qualified_frame` (the qualifier is evaluated against the exported columns, which carry each variable's full name)
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 by WP-24 on a2c7502 and on the WP-24 tree alike: `sysuse auto; dash scatter mpg weight if dis > 100, saving(...)' returns rc 0 with "if_expr filter skipped -- invalid syntax", and the page draws all 74 cars where Stata's `count if displacement > 100' selects 60.  Stata reads `dis' as displacement; dash.ado exports displacement under its full name and hands the renderer the qualifier as written, so the name it asks for is not a column.
  - Suggested fix: Expand each abbreviated variable of a qualifier to its full name in dash.ado, outside the qualifier's string literals, before the qualifier is written to the spec.
  - Resolution: Fixed 24sep2026: a qualifier is stored with each variable it abbreviates written out, outside its string literals, when the graph or KPI is registered (`_dash_qual_expand', from `_dash_process_segment', `_dash_graph_qualifier' and `_dash_kpi'), as Stata read it against the data then; `set varabbrev off' is honoured, and a scalar or any other name that is no variable is left as typed.  Certified by test/test_qualifier_literals.cscript QL-22 -- `if dis > 100' and `if make != "dis" & dis > 100' draw Stata's 60 rows in both modes, on the immediate route and as a plot's and a graph's qualifier, and a KPI's `if pri > 5000' gives Stata's sum -- each of whose three sites reverted fails it; PC-31 still holds that such a command draws, with rc 0, on both routes.

- [x] Title: A function layer naming a function Stata does not have draws nothing, where twoway refuses the command
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py at 7c28802: `GlyphMapper.map_function` (9378; its name check at 9452 raises "Unsafe name in function expression") and `_dash_report_empty_layer` (16290)
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 by WP-24's test hardening with the console binary: `dash function y = nosuchfunction(x), range(0 10), name(c)' returns rc 0, and the build draws an empty layer with the note "dash: graph 'c' plot 1 (function) drew nothing."; `twoway function y = nosuchfunction(x), range(0 10) nodraw' refuses it, "error in expression: nosuchfunction(x)", r(133) (measured again 24sep2026 with `dash function y = nosuchfunction(x), range(0 10) name(c)' and `dash build': rc 0 both).
  - Suggested fix: Refuse at registration, as twoway does, when the expression names a function outside the whitelist -- r(133), naming the function -- keeping the draw-time check for the expression text that reaches the renderer.
  - Resolution: Fixed 24sep2026 (S3 batch), recorded below; the first text of this Resolution is the historical "Not fixed" note. Not fixed: it stays open because it is a change to what dash accepts, outside test integrity.  test/test_conformance.cscript C-03 uses this layer as the control whose empty-layer note it counts, and must be given another control when this is fixed.  **Fixed 24sep2026 (S3 batch).** `_dash_fn_refuse' (dash.ado), called from `_dash_process_segment' once a function's expression is read, refuses an expression calling a name Stata has no function for, in twoway's words, "error in expression: <expression>" (echoed through `_dash_say', at most 200 characters), and with twoway's code, r(133), before anything is registered. Each name written directly before `(' outside quotes (`_dash_fn_names', dash_parse.mata, at most 100) is put to Stata as a call with 32 arguments; only an unknown function gives r(133), and nothing is evaluated (c(rngstate) unchanged). Measured 24sep2026 with the console binary: twoway refuses nosuchfunction(x), system(x), Sin(x), x*nosuch(x) + 2, the form with no `y =' and the layer inside parentheses, all r(133), and draws normal(x), max(), inlist() and sin(), rc 0. Certified by test/test_parser.cscript P1A-77 (twoway's verdict measured again on each case; the RNG state held; SMCL echoed as typed; 5,000 unknown calls refused quickly), which fails on the unfixed tree; test/test_conformance.cscript C-03's function control is now normal(x), which twoway draws and the renderer reports as an empty layer.

- [x] Title: A compound quote nested inside another is refused, where twoway accepts it
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_parse.mata at 7c28802: `_dash_quote_step` (1414), which tracks a compound quote with an on/off flag, so the first closing `"' ends the outer quote
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 by WP-24 with the console binary: `dash scatter mpg weight if make == `"say `"hi"' now"'' and `dash scatter mpg weight, title(`"a `"b"' c"')' are refused, "dash: unterminated quotation in the plot specification.", r(198); twoway accepts both, rc 0.
  - Suggested fix: Track compound-quote depth in `_dash_quote_step` instead of a flag, so each `" opens a level and each "' closes one.
  - Resolution: Fixed 24sep2026 (WP-27), recorded below; the first text of this Resolution is the historical "Not fixed" note. Not fixed: it stays open because it changes the parser every scanner shares, outside test integrity; test/test_qualifier_literals.cscript holds the literals dash reads today.  **Fixed 24sep2026 (WP-27).** `_dash_quote_step' tracks compound-quote depth instead of a flag -- each `" opens a level and each "' closes one -- so all six scanners that share it read `"a `"b"' c"' as one string. Measured 24sep2026 with the console binary: twoway accepts `if make == `"say `"hi"' now"'' and `title(`"a `"b"' c"')' (rc 0), its SVG draws a `"b"' c, it accepts 10,000 nested levels and refuses an unbalanced nesting with r(132); dash refused both with r(198). Certified by test/test_parser_integrity.cscript P1B-39..47 (every scanner, both forms through dash, a nested string holding ||, a plot command, filter( and name() that registers neither a plot nor a filter, an unbalanced nesting refused r(198) with the unterminated-quotation message, 10,000 levels stored when balanced and refused when not in 0.7 s), test/test_qualifier_literals.cscript QL-23 (the nested literal draws Stata's 23 rows on both routes and in both modes, with decoys) and test/test_json_escaping.cscript JSE-72.

- [x] Title: cert_file_has missed any needle that straddled a 32,768-character piece of a line
  - File Names and Line Numbers: test/cert_helpers.do at a2c7502: `_cert_file_has` (the fget() loop at 58)
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 by WP-24: Mata's fget() hands back a long line in pieces of 32,768 characters, and the reader searched each piece alone, so a needle across a piece boundary was never found.  A saved page is a few lines of a megabyte and more, so every one of the 423 cert_file_has calls in 37 certification scripts could miss what it looked for -- or, for an absence check, pass on what was there.
  - Suggested fix: Read the whole file, then search it.
  - Resolution: Fixed: `_cert_file_has` reads the file whole (fread in 1 MiB pieces, joined) and cert_file_count counts in the whole text.  Certified by test/test_conformance.cscript C-00, which tests the readers themselves and fails with fget() put back.

- [x] Title: Certification checks that searched a Stata log line by line depended on the length of the checkout's path
  - File Names and Line Numbers: test/test_resource_limits.cscript at a2c7502 (RL-01 to RL-13), test/test_help_claims_1.cscript (HC1-15), test/test_help_claims_3.cscript (HC3-13), test/test_help_claims_5.cscript (HC5-03)
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 by WP-24: Stata wraps a log line at the line size, anywhere, and a Python warning starts with the path to dash_render.py, so where a message broke depended on where the checkout lives.  From a 212-character path test_resource_limits failed at RL-01, and HC1-15, HC3-13 and HC5-03 failed from a 210-character path; from this checkout they passed.  The maintainer's report of 23sep2026, RL-06 failing from a long worktree path, is this defect -- which case fails first depends on the length: reproduced 24sep2026 from a 258-character path, a2c7502 failed at RL-01's wrapped needle "set global dash_max_filter_options", and 2df1900 passed RL-01 to RL-14 from the same path.
  - Suggested fix: Search a log's logical lines, with Stata's wrapped continuation lines re-joined.
  - Resolution: Fixed: cert_log_has (test/cert_helpers.do) re-joins wrapped lines and every log search in those scripts uses it.  Certified by test/test_conformance.cscript C-00 (its log reader, which fails with the re-join disabled); each script now passes from the path it failed from, and fails there again with the re-join disabled.

- [x] Title: The one-line form overwrites an existing file named by saving() without replace, and ignores replace
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado at 7c28802: `_dash_render_immediate` (writes the page saving() names with no check for an existing file; `replace' is not among its options, so it is named in the "ignoring unsupported option(s)" note)
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 by WP-24 with the console binary: with f.html holding a file of the user's, `dash scatter mpg weight, saving(f.html)' returns rc 0 and replaces it with the dashboard; `twoway scatter mpg weight, saving(f.gph)' on an existing file refuses, "already exists", r(602), and `dash build, saving(b.html)' refuses too, "dash build: file '...' already exists. Use replace option to overwrite.", r(198).  Adding replace to the one-line form changes nothing: it is reported as unsupported and ignored.
  - Suggested fix: Accept replace on the one-line form and refuse an existing file without it, with dash build's message and r(198); document it in dash.sthlp beside saving().
  - Resolution: Fixed 24sep2026 (WP-27), recorded below; the first text of this Resolution is the historical "Not fixed" note. Not fixed: it stays open because it changes what the one-line form accepts and refuses, outside test integrity; it is recorded here to be fixed first, since it can destroy a user's file.  **Fixed 24sep2026 (WP-27).** A new program, `_dash_saving_clobber', checks the file for both routes: the one-line form now refuses a file saving() names that already exists, "dash: file '...' already exists. Use replace option to overwrite.", r(198) (dash build's message and code), and writes over it given `replace' after the comma, as dash build takes it, or saving(name, replace), as twoway takes it; a directory in the file's place is refused, r(198) without replace and r(608) with it, as twoway refuses it -- in dash build too, which died in Python with r(7102) IsADirectoryError. `replace' with nothing to replace is named in the note. dash.sthlp documents it beside saving(). Measured 24sep2026 with the console binary: twoway on an existing file r(602), on a directory r(602) and with replace r(608), a bare replace r(198); dash build refuses saving(b.html, replace) with r(198). Pinned by test/test_path_validation.cscript PV-22..PV-27, whose adversarial cases -- a directory, a symbolic link to the user's file, paths holding a double quote, a dollar sign or a backtick (refused by the splitter, r(198), before the validator) -- leave the user's file untouched every time.

- [x] Title: A filter on a saved page leaves line, tsline, area, bar, spike and dropline layers, and a connected plot's line, as they were
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py at 7c28802: `map_line` (5432-5505; its `sorted_source` at 5468), `map_area` (5539-5622), `map_bar` (5624-5761), `map_spike` (5763-5821), `map_dropline` (8051-8147), `map_connected` (through `map_line`); `_build_filter_widgets` (`all_graph_sources` at 19236 holds only `self.sources`); dash.sthlp "What a filter move redraws" (1175)
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 by WP-24 at 7c28802, running the saved page's own filter callback under node: with 40 rows and a move that keeps 10, the page's scatter and dot layers go to 10, while line, tsline, area (VArea), bar (VBar), spike and dropline (Segment, and dropline's Scatter) and a connected plot's Line stay at 40, with link() and without; the served app redraws every one of them at 10.  Each of these layers draws from a copy of the columns its mapper builds, which the callback neither writes (`all_graph_sources`) nor recomputes (`agg_sources`).  dash.sthlp says the saved page "does not redraw a fitted line", implying every other layer is redrawn.
  - Suggested fix: Register each mapper-built copy with the filter callback, as computed layers are in `agg_sources`, so the script rebuilds it from the kept rows in the mapper's order (sorted by x for lines and areas), as the served app does.  A BooleanFilter view on a Line is not a fix: Bokeh rejects it (E-1024, open above).  Then parametrize test_filters.py's strict xfail over the seven types.
  - Resolution: Fixed 24sep2026 (WP-27), recorded below; the first text of this Resolution is the historical "Not fixed" note. Not fixed: it stays open because it is a change to the saved page's filter script, outside test integrity.  test/test_filters.py::TestFilterReachesTheRenderedSource::test_line_filter_updates_the_rendered_source pins the line case as a strict xfail that raises only the defect's own error, so a fix turns it into a failure to be removed with it.  **Fixed 24sep2026 (WP-27).** Every mapper that draws from a copy of the rows -- a sorted line, an area, a bar, a spike, a dropline, the range and paired-coordinate plots, a scatter without its missing rows, a layer's own labels -- carries each row's id (`__dash_row__') and draws the copy with no view; `DashRenderer._collect_derived_sources' lists the copies and `_FILTER_JS' keeps the rows of each that a move keeps, in drawn order, as `derived_sources', every column included, and recomputes a bar's or a cap's width from the kept rows (`GlyphMapper._tag_spacing'), as the served app redraws them. Certified by test/test_saved_filter_layers.py::TestEveryLayerFollowsAMove, which runs the page's own filter script under node for 23 row-drawing plot types under a dropdown, a range and a slider, with link(), by() and a layer's own if/in, and compares each figure with the saved page drawn from the kept rows (on the unfixed code 179 of the file's 250 tests fail), ::TestTheLineFollowsTheMoveAsTwowayDraws and ::TestTheSpacingTag, and by test/test_filters.py::TestFilterReachesTheRenderedSource::test_line_filter_updates_the_rendered_source, whose strict xfail is removed, now over seven types. The range and paired-coordinate plots had the same defect and are fixed the same way; rbar now draws from its own rows, so a linked selection no longer highlights it on the saved page, as in the served app (dash.sthlp updated). A variable named __proto__ lost its column on every filter move; columns are now created as the object's own properties (adversarial test in the same file).

- [x] Title: A range layer with no second y variable is reported as a plot type with no glyph mapper
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py at 7c28802: `_dash_add_glyph` (16472-16488)
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 by WP-24: a spec whose rscatter, rarea or rcap layer gives `yvar1' and no `yvar2' draws nothing and warns "dash: no glyph mapper for plot type 'rscatter'; nothing was drawn for that layer." -- false: the mapper exists, and the missing second y variable is the cause; the empty-layer report follows it.  Only a spec written by hand reaches this: dash.ado always writes `yvar2'.
  - Suggested fix: When the type is a range type and its second y variable is empty, say that the layer names no second y variable.
  - Resolution: Fixed 24sep2026 (S3 batch), recorded below; the first text of this Resolution is the historical "Not fixed" note. Not fixed: it stays open because it is a change to what the renderer reports, outside test integrity, and dash.ado never writes such a spec.  **Fixed 24sep2026 (S3 batch).** For a spec that reaches the renderer with a range layer naming no second y variable, both modes now say so, in the same words -- "dash: a 'rscatter' layer takes two y variables and an x variable, and this one names no second y variable; nothing was drawn for that layer." (`_dash_note_no_second_y', called by `_dash_add_glyph' and the served range branch, the type quoted by repr()); "no glyph mapper" stays for a type that has none. Pinned by test/test_layer_reports.py::TestARangeLayerWithNoSecondY (rscatter, rarea and rcap in each mode, the same wording, a full range layer still drawn, an unknown type still "no glyph mapper", a hostile type quoted). This entry's belief that dash.ado never writes such a spec was wrong: measured 24sep2026, `dash rscatter mpg weight' reaches the renderer with the x variable empty and stops in a Python traceback, r(7102), where twoway refuses "rscatter requires 3 variables: mpg weight", r(102) -- the open entry "dash rscatter, rarea or rcap given two variables stops in a Python traceback, where twoway refuses it with r(102)".

- [x] Title: BOKEH_ALLOW_WS_ORIGIN replaced the served app's websocket origin list without a word
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py at 7c28802: the generated launcher's `__main__` block (22507-22545) and `_dash_server_app` (22455-22505, `allow_websocket_origin=_origins` at 22500); dash.sthlp's Security section (1222-1234); bokeh 3.9 server/views/ws.py `WSHandler.check_origin` (113)
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 by WP-24 with a running app and the handshake a browser makes: Bokeh's websocket handler uses the variable, when it is set, instead of the list the app passes it.  Set to another host, the app refused localhost and 127.0.0.1 -- the page at the address the launcher printed stayed blank -- and --allow-websocket-origin did nothing; set to `*', every origin opened a session, http://attacker.example included, so any web site the user visited while the dashboard ran could read what it draws.  Nothing was printed, and dash.sthlp's Security section never named the variable.  CLAUDE.md rule 15 asks for environment variables to be verified at start-up.
  - Suggested fix: Read the variable when the launcher starts and say what it does; refuse `*', or add the variable's origins to the app's own list instead -- a choice of policy.
  - Resolution: Fixed as far as the silence: the launcher reads the variable at start, prints that Bokeh admits its origins instead of the app's list, naming them, and warns when it holds `*' that any web site can open a session; dash.sthlp's Security section says the same.  The replacement itself is Bokeh's rule and stays the operator's choice, as WP-20 pinned it ("An operator who sets it owns the origin policy"); whether dash should refuse `*', or treat the variable's origins as additions, is left to the maintainer.  Certified by test/test_adversarial_matrix.py::TestSessionOrigin::test_bokeh_lets_the_environment_replace_it (the note names the variable and what it admits; the app without it says nothing) and ::test_a_star_in_the_environment_is_warned_of, both of which fail without the note.

- [x] Title: Any dash command holding a double quote followed by an apostrophe stopped at the entry, before anything was stored
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado at 2df1900: the `dash` entry (95 `regexm(`"`0'"', ...)', 100 `_args = substr(`"`0'"', ...)'), and the UTF-8 gates `mata: _dash_check_utf8(strtrim(`"`0'"'))' in `_dash_plot' (3398, with `_dash_split_segs' at 3401), `_dash_kpi' (4335), `_dash_prepare_spec' (4644), `_dash_build' (5204), `_dash_serve_spec' (5381) and `_dash_serve' (5473)
  - Description: Measured 24sep2026 at 2df1900 with the console binary: each site put the whole command inside compound quotes in a Stata expression or a Mata line, and a text holding "' -- one that opens with an apostrophe inside double quotes, title("'90s cars"), or a qualifier's literal "' or 1 or '" -- ended those quotes early.  A graph title or qualifier stopped with r(3000), `dash kpi mean(price), title("'90s price") name(k)' and `dash build, title("'90s cars")' with r(100) ") required", their compound-quoted forms with r(133), a KPI qualifier with r(198); nothing was registered.  twoway itself refuses the plain-quoted forms on this machine, r(109) "type mismatch", under version 16 to 19, and draws the compound-quoted ones; dash now stores the text in both forms, as the maintainer asked, and each test's comment records twoway's r(109).

Certified by test/test_json_escaping.cscript JSE-50 (a KPI title, plain and compound, stored and drawn as typed), JSE-53 (a dashboard title) and JSE-54 (dash serve), each failing at 2df1900; the graph cases, which also needed the plot chain's own sites (the entry below), are JSE-42..49.

- [x] Title: A plot command stopped, or stored its text cut, when a title, text option, value or qualifier held a double quote followed by an apostrophe
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado at 2df1900: `_dash_process_segment' (2557 `args', 2617, 2620, 2624, 2687, 2736, 2922), `_dash_graph_qualifier' (1258-1259), `_dash_plot' (3419, 3438, 3451, 3491-3496, 3655), `_dash_register_graph' (3915, 3936), `_dash_validate_value' (1672), `_dash_check_legend' (1494, 1498), `_dash_report_ignored' (3349), `_dash_validate_opts' (2112-2113, 2132-2133), the option parsers' emptiness tests (from 666 and from 903), the varlist parsers (1133, 1150, 1167, 1184, 1224)

- [x] Title: The renderer skipped `if !x' and `if ~x' on a numeric column, and drew every row
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py at 2df1900: `_stata_if_to_pandas' (10877-10879, which wrote Stata's ! as pandas' ~), `_dash_qualified_frame' (16209-16218)
  - Description: Reported 23sep2026 at c0200c0 and measured 24sep2026 at 2df1900 on sysuse auto: `if !foreign' and `if ~foreign' failed in pandas ("ufunc 'invert' not supported"), so the qualifier was skipped with a warning and both modes drew 74 cars, where Stata's count selects 52.  Stata's not is defined on numbers: nonzero is true, and so is missing, so !x is true exactly where x == 0; ! binds tighter than any comparison (`!foreign == 1' is `(!foreign) == 1'), and a sign right after it (`!-x') is Stata's r(198).
  - Suggested fix: Translate a not on a numeric operand as ~(x != 0), with Stata's precedence.
  - Resolution: Fixed: `_stata_logic_to_pandas' reads the qualifier's logic in one pass by Stata's precedence and truth, and writes a number wherever a true/false value belongs as (x != 0), which is true for a missing value, as in Stata.  Certified by test/test_qualifier_logic.py `TestEachModeDrawsStatasRows' (36 not-cases in both modes), `TestAKpiSumsStatasRows', `TestAFilterMoveKeepsTheQualifier' and `TestTheTranslation', and test/test_qualifier_literals.cscript QL-16 to QL-19, each failing with the fix reverted (74 carried where Stata selects 52; a KPI 2775 where Stata sums 1378; two panels where twoway draws one).

- [x] Title: Under Bokeh 3.8, the served app admitted a websocket origin whose host only begins with an allowed one
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py at 3130fba: the generated launcher's `_dash_server_app' (the `allow_websocket_origin=_origins' it hands Bokeh's Server, at 23123); Bokeh 3.8.0's `bokeh/server/util.py' `match_host' (166-235), which `check_allowlist' (101) calls for `bokeh/server/views/ws.py''s `check_origin' (115)
  - Description: Found 24sep2026 by running the pytest suite under Stata's own interpreter (WP-25's TR-25.2): `/opt/anaconda3/bin/python3', Python 3.13.9 with bokeh 3.8.0, the one every `dash serve' on this machine runs.  test/test_adversarial_matrix.py::TestSessionOrigin::test_a_foreign_origin_is_refused failed for `http://localhost.evil.example:<port>' and `http://127.0.0.1.nip.io:<port>': the app answered the browser's handshake 101 and ACK, a session opened, where the development interpreter's bokeh 3.9.0 refuses both, 403.  Bokeh 3.8's matcher compares only as many dot-separated labels as the allowed pattern has, so `localhost.evil.example' matches `localhost' and `127.0.0.1.nip.io' matches `127.0.0.1'; bokeh 3.9 requires the label counts to be equal.  A page served from a DNS name that begins with localhost, or from a rebinding service's name for 127.0.0.1, could open a session with the dashboard and read every observation it embeds.  The development suite never saw it: it runs bokeh 3.9.
  - Suggested fix: Check origins label for label in dash, whatever Bokeh the app runs under.
  - Resolution: Fixed: `_dash_strict_match_host' holds Bokeh 3.9's rules, and `_dash_harden_origin_check', which the launcher calls before it builds its Server, puts it in the place of Bokeh's `match_host' when Bokeh's own admits a host it must refuse -- the matcher's one caller path is the websocket origin check -- and the launcher says so; dash.sthlp's Security section says it, and that `bokeh serve app.py' keeps Bokeh's own check.  Certified by test/test_adversarial_matrix.py::TestSessionOriginUnderALenientBokeh, which runs the app with Bokeh 3.8's matcher planted in its process, so the development interpreter holds the fix too (all five fail with the launcher's call removed), and ::TestTheStrictHostMatcher; TestSessionOrigin passes under Stata's interpreter again.

  - Description: Found 24sep2026 by running the pytest suite under Stata's own interpreter (WP-25's TR-25.2), /opt/anaconda3/bin/python3 with bokeh 3.8.0: (1) the single-y page's hash differed from its baseline, and the only difference in the normalised document was the Bokeh version it records ("version":"3.8.0" for "3.9.0"), so the guard was a Bokeh version check, the thing its normaliser says it must not be; (2) the long-qualifier exhaustion case took 11.1 s against a 10 s bound, where the translation itself takes 1.3 s under Python 3.13: the time was taken inside tracemalloc, whose bookkeeping costs four times as much there as under Python 3.14; (3) the text-sink safety pins were verified only on bokeh 3.9.0, so TestBokehVersion refused 3.8.0, as it should until someone checks.

Layers computed from a date column -- fits, histograms, areas, range layers -- were drawn in nanoseconds (pandas 2.3) or microseconds (3.0) against a millisecond axis, and a missing date at -9.2e18; pcarrow and pcbarrow crashed on a date, a bar over dates was 0.8 ms wide, dropline's mlabel(date) printed ".", the KPI script wrote a year below 1000 in three digits, and a date's sum() wrapped.   - Description: Found 24sep2026 by WP-27's responsive check (TR-27.2), measured in headless Chrome through an iframe exactly 375 px wide. examples/geometry_responsive.do (layout(bs)) kept its by(foreign) facet panels side by side at 266 px each -- a page 545 px wide, one figure offscreen -- though dash.sthlp says that under layout(bs) "below 768 every item takes the whole row"; examples/full_dashboard.do (layout(3 2)) kept two 220 px columns, 440 px wide, two figures offscreen. Every gridplot() grid left its CSS columns at auto, so no column could be narrower than its figure's natural minimum, about 220 px: a 1 x 4 grid, a by(, cols(4)) facet grid and a facet inside a tab overflowed a 768 px window the same way (880 and 1228 px). The filter bar did not wrap (411 px at 375), filterposition(left) kept its 240 px sidebar beside the grid (405 px, figures 135 px), and in the served layout(bs) grid beside the sidebar the KPI cards' fixed 160 px minimum made the page 813 px wide at 768.
  - Suggested fix: Give every grid equal shrinkable columns and stack a grid of n columns into one when it is narrower than n x 240 px (a container query on the grid itself); stack the served layout(bs) GridBox below a 768 px window; wrap the filter bar; stack the sidebar row below 768 px; let a KPI card narrow below 160 px; in both modes.
  - Resolution: Fixed (WP-27). `_dash_reflow' gives each gridplot() grid cols minmax(0, 1fr) and an inline stylesheet that stacks it into one column, in reading order, when it is narrower than ncols x 240 px -- so a facet grid inside a narrow cell or tab stacks while the grid around it keeps its columns; the served layout(bs) GridBox keeps its spans down to a 768 px window and then stacks; the filter bar wraps; the filterposition(left) row stacks below 768 px; KPI cards take min-width:min(160px,100%), in the Python card and its JS rebuild alike. dash.sthlp describes the behaviour at phone width, and that the served app on a real phone lays out at desktop width, declaring no viewport. Pinned by test/test_responsive_layout.py::TestPagesFitInChrome::test_saved_page_fits (11 layout families rendered from specs, each measured in headless Chrome at 375, 768 and 1440 px: no page wider than its window, nothing offscreen or overlapping, every figure at least 200 px wide and 100 tall; without Chrome it skips, which fails a DASH_STRICT=1 run), ::TestServedDocumentsFitInChrome::test_served_document_fits (6 families), ::TestTheProbe, ::TestReflowModel, ::TestReflowAdversarial, ::TestEveryGridIsReflowed and ::TestKpiCardMayNarrow; on the unfixed code 10 of the 11 saved families and all 6 served ones failed. Measured on the Stata-built example pages after the fix: geometry_responsive is 375 px wide at 375 (figures 351 px) and full_dashboard 375 (figures 375 px), bs_responsive, bs_stacked and bs_kpi_hero unchanged, every page with nothing offscreen or overlapping at all three widths.

- [x] Title: A string value holding an unclosed compound quote, a lone backtick or apostrophe, or the closing pair stops every export inside jsonio; every strL is exported as "null"
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado: the jsonio export on the one-line route (`jsonio out' of the needed variables) and on the `_dash_prepare_spec' route (`jsonio out' of all variables); jsonio.ado lines 55 and 307-310, which expand the JSON written in compound quotes; now `_dash_write_data' and dash_render.py's `_dash_write_stata_data'
  - Description: Found 24sep2026 by WP-27's quoting work (JSE-72's decoys) and measured on 5 observations of auto with mlabel(s): jsonio's Java writes the file, but its ado then returns the JSON in a macro and expands it inside compound quotes, so a string value, value label or variable label that leaves them unbalanced stops the export whatever the qualifier -- `" or a lone backtick r(132) "too few quotes", "' or a lone apostrophe r(109); $, \, ", CR/LF, control bytes, multibyte UTF-8, `c1' and `=1+1' round-tripped. jsonio also wrote every strL as the text "null", flagged numeric, so a strL column arrived empty.
  - Suggested fix: Write the data file without jsonio, reading each value through the Stata Function Interface.
  - Resolution: Fixed (WP-27). dash.ado's `_dash_write_data' writes the data file from Stata's Python through dash_render.py's `_dash_write_stata_data', which reads every value through sfi, in jsonio's layout (missing numbers "null", every number a double, value labels keyed by variable, jsonio's codes for .a-.z labels); no value passes through a macro, the path and names reach Python through Macro.getLocal, names are checked to be Stata names before any command is built from them, a strL exports as a string, invalid UTF-8 is read through ustrfix() (U+FFFD, as jsonio wrote it) with a note naming where, a binary strL is refused r(198), and dash no longer calls jsonio. Measured in Stata: every str# and strL value, variable label and value label of test/test_string_values.cscript -- 24 adversarial values alone and together, a 1 MB strL, labels holding quotes, every storage type, missing values and dates -- reaches both the saved renderer's frame and the served app's `_load_spec_and_data()' byte for byte (SV-01..SV-04, SV-08; on the old code SV-01 fails at its first value, r(132)); invalid UTF-8 SV-06; a binary strL SV-07; a build with jsonio off the ado-path and out of memory SV-09. Also pinned by test/test_string_value_export.py::TestTheWriter, ::TestTheLabelKey, ::TestBothRenderersLoadEveryValueExactly::test_saved_and_served, ::TestThePageCarriesNoValueAsMarkup::test_a_script_end_in_a_value_stays_inside_the_json and ::TestDashAdoUsesTheWriter. A 1e5-row, 7-column export is no slower (warm 0.20-0.51 s against jsonio's 0.33-0.59 s).

- [x] Title: No byte cap on the exported data: a strL dataset makes an unbounded page
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado: `_dash_limit_table', the one-line form's and build/serve's exports; dash_render.py: `_DASH_LIMITS', the saved renderer's and `ServerAppBuilder''s loads; now `_dash_byte_cap', `_dash_text_bytes', `_dash_refuse_overbytes'
  - Description: Found 24sep2026 by WP-27, once dash's own writer exported strL values in full (jsonio had written each as "null"). $dash_max_cells counts values, not bytes: 60 observations of a 1,000,000-byte strL were 60 values, far inside the cells limit, and 60 MB of page.
  - Suggested fix: Add a bytes limit to the WP-19 table, enforced in Stata before the file is written and in the renderer for a data file that arrives another way.
  - Resolution: Fixed (WP-27). $dash_max_bytes limits the bytes of text in the string values exported, as Stata stores them, strL included: default 50,000,000, ceiling 500,000,000, a bad value refused through `_dash_limit' as the other limits refuse one. Over it both routes stop with r(134) before the file is written, in the cells cap's words ("dash: this dashboard would embed N bytes of text (in K string variables), more than the L dash embeds." and the same remedy). Nothing is read when every string variable is a str# whose width times _N fits; otherwise the lengths are summed in Mata a million observations at a time; the renderer counts only a data file larger than the limit. Measured in Stata: auto's make holds 871 bytes (the sum of strlen), refused under a limit of 870 and built under 871; 60 x 1,000,000-byte strL refused at the default and 50 admitted; a 100,000-row build is within 1% of its time before (median of 5). Pinned by test/test_adversarial.cscript P19-27..P19-30 and P19-05/18/19/20 (now eight limits), test/test_resource_limits.py::TestTheBytesOfTextAreLimited and ::TestTheTwoLanguagesAgree::test_the_help_documents_every_limit_with_its_numbers, registered in test/test_adversarial_matrix.py.

- [x] Title: sort on a line plot is named as an unsupported option, where dash draws what sort asks for
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado: the option table the "ignoring unsupported option(s)" note is built from; dash.sthlp, "Connection order"
  - Description: Found 24sep2026 by WP-27's release gate: `dash line price weight, name(g2) sort' prints "dash: ignoring unsupported option(s): sort()". dash.sthlp says dash always joins a line's points in the order of x, which is the picture twoway draws with sort, so the page is what sort asks for and the note says it was ignored; sort(varlist), which dash does not honour, is rightly noted.
  - Suggested fix: Accept a bare sort on the connected types without a note, keeping the note for sort(varlist).
  - Resolution: Fixed 24sep2026 (S3 batch), recorded below; the first text of this Resolution is the historical "Not fixed" note. Not fixed: it stays open because it changes what the option table accepts, found by the gate's own test case after every S1 and S2 entry was closed.  **Fixed 24sep2026 (S3 batch).** A bare sort on line, connected, area, tsline, rline, rarea, rconnected or tsrline -- the types dash always joins in the order of x (map_line, map_area, map_rline, map_rarea), the picture twoway draws with sort -- is no longer named in the ignoring note (`_dash_fold_typed'); on another type a bare sort is still named, and sort(varlist) on every type (`_dash_parse_plot_opts'). dash.sthlp's "Connection order" says so. Measured 24sep2026: twoway accepts sort, rc 0, on the eight types and on scatter and bar. Certified by test/test_twoway_option_parity.cscript TP-06b (the eight types, paren mode, and the scatter, bar and sort(varlist) controls, twoway's verdict measured again), which fails 9 checks on the unfixed tree; TP-06 still holds `sort sort(mpg)' named once.

- [x] Title: An unresolvable #include note is printed twice by one dash scatter build
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py: `DashRenderer.__init__' and `DashRenderer._make_figure', which each parsed the scheme; `SchemeParser._include', where the note is raised; now `DashRenderer._scheme_for'
  - Description: Found 24sep2026 by the S3 batch, once an #include that resolves nowhere was noted as Stata notes it. Measured in Stata with b2inc.scheme holding `#include b2nosuch': `twoway scatter mpg weight, scheme(b2inc) nodraw' prints "(note: scheme b2nosuch not found, using s2color)" once; `dash scatter mpg weight, scheme(b2inc)' printed it twice, as did a registered graph with scheme() and then dash build, while dash build, scheme() (saved and served) printed it once. On the one-line route the graph's scheme() is also the build's, so __init__ parsed the file for the build and _make_figure again for the graph, and the catch_warnings blocks between them reset Python's duplicate suppression. S3: a note repeated.
  - Suggested fix: Parse each scheme name once per build.
  - Resolution: Fixed (S3 batch). `DashRenderer._scheme_for' keeps the renderer's parsed schemes by name, so each scheme is read once per build and each of its notes printed once; a second build notes it again; two different unresolvable includes still give two notes, and a graph scheme other than the build's is still noted. Pinned by test/test_immediate_scheme.py::TestAnIncludeNoteIsPrintedOncePerBuild (the one-line route, a build and a graph scheme, a graph scheme other than the build's, two builds, the served builder, and 50 graphs naming one scheme parsed once) and test/test_custom_scheme.cscript CS-15, which counts each note's lines in the log against twoway's -- the one-line route, a registered graph, dash build saved and served -- and failed with "found 2" on the unfixed tree.

- [x] Title: Shipped schemes spell out symbol p1..p15, so a user's symbol p (and symbolsize p#) does not reach the plots Stata's scheme chain reaches
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py: `SchemeParser._init_properties' (p_symbols, now p_marker_sizes), `default_marker_size'; scripts/extract_scheme_truth.py; schemes/*.scheme; test/fixtures/scheme_truth.json
  - Description: Found 24sep2026 by the S3 batch's scheme-chain fix. Measured in Stata for all 20 shipped schemes under `#include S' and one more line, reading plots 1 and 2's marker symbol and size from the graph object: `symbol p diamond' makes both markers diamonds in 11 schemes and leaves circle and diamond in the 9 whose chain declares symbol p1..p15 itself (stmono1, stmono2, stsj, s2mono, s1mono, sj, s2manual, s1manual, s2gmanual); `symbol p1' or `symbol p2 diamond' changes that plot alone in all 20; `symbolsize p1 huge' plot 1 alone; `symbolsize p huge' both plots in 19, s1manual keeping 2.2 because its file declares symbolsize p1..p9. dash's shipped files wrote symbol p1..p15, which Stata's files never write, so a bare symbol p did nothing in the 11; and dash read symbolsize p alone, so symbolsize p1 was ignored and under s1manual symbolsize p huge drew huge markers where Stata keeps 2.2. S3: custom-scheme fidelity.
  - Suggested fix: Follow symbol p# to symbol p and symbolsize p# to symbolsize p in the parser; have the shipped files carry only the keys Stata's chain declares.
  - Resolution: Fixed (S3 batch). `p_symbols' follows symbol p# to symbol p, the new `p_marker_sizes' symbolsize p# to symbolsize p, and `default_marker_size(index)' gives each plot its own size, cycling through 15; the extractor writes only the symbol and symbolsize keys Stata declares and removes spelled-out symbol p# lines; regenerated, 11 files carry symbol p circle where they wrote p1..p15 and s1manual gains symbolsize p1..p9 2.2, every shipped scheme drawing the symbols and sizes it drew. Pinned by test/test_scheme_consumption.py::TestAChildSymbolReachesWhatStatasChainReaches (a bare symbol p, a symbol p#, the symbols each shipped file draws, the keys each declares -- each for all 20 -- and a hostile value) and ::TestAChildSymbolsizeReachesWhatStatasChainReaches (a bare symbolsize p, symbolsize p1, the sizes each file draws, a wrapping index and a hostile size).

- [x] Title: linewidth p# in a custom scheme is not read: every plot's line takes linewidth p
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py: `SchemeParser.default_line_width' and the drawing sites that read it
  - Description: Found 24sep2026 by the S3 batch's symbol-chain measurement. In Stata, a custom scheme's `linewidth p1 vthick' after `#include s2color' thickens plot 1's line alone (0.3 to 1.4, read from the graph object), and linewidth p#line has no effect; dash has one line width, from linewidth p, shared by about 30 drawing sites, so linewidth p1 is ignored. No shipped file spells the key out, so the shipped schemes draw as Stata does; a user's scheme that sets it does not.
  - Suggested fix: Follow linewidth p# to linewidth p per plot, as the colour, pattern, symbol and size chains now do, at every site that draws a plot's line.
  - Resolution: Fixed 24sep2026 (S3 batch), recorded below; the first text of this Resolution is the historical "Not fixed" note. Not fixed: it stays open because it was found after the batch's fixes landed.  **Fixed 24sep2026 (S3 batch).** A custom scheme's linewidth p# reaches plot #'s line through Stata's chain linewidth p#<kind> -> p<kind> -> p# -> p (`SchemeParser.plot_line_width', the plot index cycling through 15), at every site that draws a plot's line, in both modes. Measured 24sep2026 with StataNow 19.5 over 196 two-plot graphs under 10 custom schemes, reading .Graph.plotregion1.plot<k>.style.line.width and .style.area.linestyle.width (test/fixtures/linewidth_chain_truth.json): under #include s2color, linewidth p1 vthick and linewidth p2 thick, plots 1 and 2 are 1.4 and .8 on every line-bearing type. The kind is the style file's: lineplot for line, the fits, kdensity, function, rline and a ci fit's line; area for the area and rarea outlines; arrowline for pcarrow and pcbarrow; plain p# for connected, the spikes and caps, dropline, rconnected, pcspike, pccapsym, mspline and mband; a bar stops at linewidth pbar, which every Stata scheme sets; ci bands and histograms take their own keys; linewidth p1line reaches nothing. Every shipped scheme draws the widths it drew, but for the pc* and rcapsym lines, hard-coded at 1.5 px, which now take linewidth p like every other plot -- under economist 6.0 px (1.2 units), as Stata draws them. Pinned by test/test_scheme_linewidth.py::TestTheChainAgainstStata::test_each_measured_plot, ::TestTheChainByKey (with test_the_shipped_file_draws_the_widths_it_drew), ::TestAdversarial and ::TestBothModesDrawEachPlotsWidth (test_linewidth_p1_and_p2, test_a_bar_takes_pbar_not_p1, test_economist_draws_its_pc_lines_at_linewidth_p); 261 of its 273 tests failed on the unfixed code.

- [x] Title: A repeated option kept its first copy and was named as unsupported, where twoway takes the last copy, merges the copies, or refuses a unique one
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado: `_dash_parse_graph_opts' and `_dash_parse_plot_opts' (-syntax-'s * catch-all), `_dash_process_segment' (the graph-option accumulator it overwrote), `_dash_plot' (the after-comma value copied over); dash_render.py: `_dash_reference_lines' (every xline()/yline() position drawn in one style); now `_dash_opts_repeats', dash_parse.mata's `_dash_rep_*', `_dash_refline_instances', `_dash_refline_draw'
  - Description: Found 24sep2026 by the S3 batch's option-parity fix. twoway reads a repeated option three ways (measured from its SVG exports, as repeated_options.sthlp says): the last copy wins for most options (`mcolor(red) mcolor(blue)' and `mc(red) mcolor(blue)' draw blue, and an earlier bad value is never read); the copies merge for titles, axis labels and ticks, legend(), xscale()/yscale(), the regions, by(), xline()/yline() and text() (`title(A) title(, color(red))' is A in red, `xlabel(2000 3000) xlabel(4000, add)' labels all three); and a unique option -- name, saving, scheme, aspectratio, xsize, ysize, nodraw, yaxis, a bare sort, kernel and bwidth on the smoothers, and others -- refuses its second copy, "option scheme() not allowed", r(198). -syntax- bound the first copy and put later ones in the catch-all, named as unsupported; `title(A) title(B)' bound the second to title2() and a second xlabel() went to xlabel2(), the second axis, in silence; a later plot group's graph option overwrote an earlier one's, so legend(label(1 ..)) in one group was lost beside legend(label(2 ..)) after the comma, with no note; and unique options given twice were accepted. Measured against twoway on the unfixed code: 31 of 33 commands stored otherwise than the command twoway draws alike (16 with a misleading note, the rest silent), and all 12 unique-option cases accepted. S1 for the silent forms.
  - Suggested fix: Rebuild the option list as twoway reads it before the parsed values are used: last copy, merged copies or a refusal, by option, and merge graph options across segments by the same rule.
  - Resolution: Fixed (S3 batch). `_dash_opts_repeats' (dash.ado) and dash_parse.mata's `_dash_rep_*' run after each parse: when a spelling repeats or one is a prefix of another, each distinct spelling (at most 100) is put to the parser alone to learn which option it is, and the list is rewritten with one copy of each -- the last, or the copies merged by twoway's rule (a later text replaces, sub-options merge keeping the last of each, suffix, prefix and add honoured, an xscale range() the union) -- a unique option given twice refused in twoway's words, r(198); the list is parsed once more, so no note names a repeat. `_dash_plot' merges graph options from plot groups, || segments and after the comma in that order and refuses a unique option given in more than one place; the renderer draws each xline()/yline() copy in its own style. twoway's ceiling of 256 options holds: 10,000 copies are r(1003) in both. Pinned by test/test_twoway_option_parity.cscript TP-14a (33 command pairs, twoway's SVGs compared in the run), TP-14b (12 refusals, sort and sort(varlist) in either order), TP-14c (the one-line route and name() then dash build), TP-14d (repeated yline() copies kept apart) and TP-14e (10,000 copies, 255 options in under 10 s, a hostile value stored as escaped text, an unbindable copy still refused), by test/test_axis_options.py::TestRepeatedReferenceLines and test/test_alias_semantics.cscript AS-06b.

- [x] Title: A function layer with a blank before a parenthesis, function y = sin (x), was drawn where twoway refuses it

- [x] Title: A scheme's quoted values (RGB colours, %opacity) were dropped without a warning
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py SchemeParser._parse_lines (tokens[-1] as the value)
  - Description: GAPS2 D1's measured symptom: `color background "255 0 0"' was stored under a malformed key, so the directive was lost without a warning; a scheme written with quoted RGB drew every series in its `color p' default instead, with 0 warnings; the same reader stored every shipped scheme's `label "s2 color"' line under the key `label "s2', and never skipped a `sequence' line.
  - Suggested fix: Tokenise a scheme line as Stata's own scheme.class does: the value is the third token with its quotes removed, later tokens are ignored, `sequence' and `label' lines are skipped, and a line that cannot be read that way is named once, bounded, with its file and line number.
  - Resolution: Fixed 25sep2026 (WP-28, D1). SchemeParser._parse_lines tokenises a line as scheme.class does (_scheme_tokens: a quoted or compound-quoted string is one token, quotes stripped, the third token is the value, sequence and label lines are skipped, an unreadable line is named once with its bounded file name and line number), in both renderers through _SCHEME_PROPS. - [x] Title: The data limit counts exported values, so large histograms, densities and fits are refused although the page would be small
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado: `_dash_cell_cap', `_dash_prepare_spec', `_dash_render_immediate'; dash_parse.mata: `_dash_computed_cells', `_dash_computed_plot_cells', `_dash_graph_touched', `_dash_qual_cols_in', `_dash_filter_excludes'; dash_render.py: `_dash_embedded_cells', `_dash_refuse_oversized', `_report_dataset_shape'
  - Description: GAPS2 G3: the limits exist so nothing "can grow without bound" (dash.sthlp), but `_dash_cell_cap' counted `_N' times every variable exported plus every qualifier column, whatever the page would actually hold. `dash histogram x' on 5,000,001 observations was r(134) by default, and nothing could be drawn past 20,000,000 observations, although the saved page embeds a histogram's bars, not its rows.
  - Suggested fix: Count what the saved page embeds -- a graph made only of computed layers (histogram, kdensity, a fit or a smoother) that no filter(), link(), csv or hover() reaches draws its own bounded output; every other graph, every KPI card and every filter variable counts its columns times the observations, as before. Keep the served app's full count and the JSON export unchanged.
  - Resolution: Fixed 25sep2026 (WP-28, G3). `_dash_computed_cells' and `_dash_graph_touched' (dash_parse.mata) decide, per graph, whether it draws only its own computed output and whether a filter, link(), csv or hover() reaches its rows; `_dash_cell_cap' (dash.ado) grows an `extra' and a `served' argument so its message names the drawn output, a mixed count, or a served app's full count, byte-identical to before when neither applies; `_dash_prepare_spec' and `_dash_render_immediate' build `row_vars'/`comp_cells' beside the unchanged `all_vars' export list, and the server route (`dash build, server' or `dash serve') keeps the full count. `_dash_embedded_cells', the extra keyword of `_dash_refuse_oversized' and `_report_dataset_shape', and the `_DASH_COMPUTED_ONLY_TYPES'/`_DASH_COMPUTED_PLOT_CELLS' constants (dash_render.py) are the renderer's twin, called from `DashRenderer.__init__' and `render()' (saved) and unconditionally, before the served builder embeds anything, in `ServerAppBuilder.build' for the string-variable check the same commit's G2 half added. Measured once, not a committed test: `clear; set obs 6000000; generate double x = rnormal()' then `dash histogram x, bin(50)' built a 1,441,675-byte page with rc 0, and `dash scatter x x' was r(134) ("this dashboard would embed 6,000,000 values (6,000,000 observations x 1 variable), more than the 5,000,000 dash embeds"). Pinned by test/test_embedded_cells.py (`TestTheCount', `TestTheRefusalAndTheNote', `TestBothModes', `TestTheTwoLanguagesAgree'), test/test_adversarial.cscript DL-01..DL-06. Residual, deferred (WP-28): a by()-faceted graph is never treated as computed-only and is counted in full, as it was before this section -- the actual panel count is not known before the export, and multiplying the generic 120,000-cell bound by the by_groups LIMIT (100 by default) would read a two-panel by(foreign) on a plain kdensity or lpoly as 12,000,000, over the default cells limit on any dataset however small, which measurably regressed test/test_help_claims_6.py's by()-faceted lpoly grid before this residual was chosen; the export still writes every observation as JSON (DISCOVERY Q9), row-drawing layers, filters, link(), csv and hover() stay bounded by the limit, and the served app embeds every row.
- [x] Title: dash serve returns rc 0 when no server ran, and an out-of-range --port is clamped instead of refused
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py (the --launch block 27670-27715 at 91d97be, the clamps at 27371, 27603 and 27680, `_dash_arg_parser'), dash.ado (`_dash_serve' 7349-7439)
  - Description: Measured 25sep2026 (GAPS2 F1): probing with the port held by another socket returned rc 0 after 1.7 s -- the only trace was the child's own `OSError: [Errno 48] Address already in use' on process stderr, which never reached Stata; a leftover app.py on the default port made a new `dash serve' "succeed" while the browser showed the old dashboard. Separately, `python app.py --port 80' served on 1024 because of the clamp in the app's own `__main__', and two more clamps (`main()', the launcher) moved any out-of-range port to the nearest bound instead of refusing it.

  - Description: GAPS2 B2 (S1, measured at 91d97be): explicit ticks only set a FixedTicker, so `ylabel(0(20)100)` on mpg 12-41 never showed 60-100; `_dash_apply_scale_ranges` set `Range1d(lo, hi)` exactly before any layer was drawn, so `yscale(range(100))` drew an inverted axis (100 to 41), `range(20 30)` hid the data outside 20-30, `range(0)` ended exactly at the data maximum, and `reverse` beside `range()` was dropped; `yscale(r(0 100))`, `yscale(rev)` and `norescale` were named as not implemented; the served app autoranged over a fit's 10%-extended grid where the saved page did not. twoway's rule (axis_label_options.sthlp:344-350, axis_scale_options.sthlp:144-148, 336-341): label and tick values widen the axis unless norescale, and range() only ever widens. Measured against twoway (test/fixtures/axis_truth.json, group b2_extent, 27 probes): twoway drops norescale from a lone a(b)c rule (the .gph records `.major.range_ticks 0 100 20` with no norescale) and widens that axis exactly as without it, while a list keeps norescale (`.add_ticks ..., norescale`) and is not widened.   - Suggested fix: Decide the extent after the layers, as the hull of the drawn data, the label and tick positions (unless norescale) and every range() value, with dash's padding, in both modes; read range() as a numlist of values to include; share the primary-renderers limit between the saved page and the served app.
  - Resolution: Fixed 30sep2026 (WP-28, B2). After the layers, every axis with an explicit label, tick or range() value spans the hull of its data (a bar's full width included), its positions (unless norescale, which twoway drops from a lone a(b)c rule) and its range() values, padded 5% a side in log or date units, reversed on request, shared across by() panels, on the second axes too; #N ticks are placed over the widened scale; range() is read as a numlist (r(), rev, missing values ignored, a non-number named once); and both renderers limit their autoranges to the same renderers, through _dash_axis_hull, _dash_padded_range, _dash_hull_ranges and _dash_limit_ranges_to_primary in both renderers. - [x] Title: The served app has no credential, so any local account can open a session and read the data
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py at 7421d3d: ServerAppBuilder (28242; the emitted make_document at 29994), main (31888), _dash_launch_app (31944)
  - Description: DROPIN-REMAINING.md P0.12, verified at 357c368: the served app has no credential. Any local account can open a session and read the data. The help's "only this machine" wording understates this. Sources: GAPS2-I3-a, GAPS2-I3-c, AUDIT-87.
  - Suggested fix: WP-29 section 13 (served-app token): require a per-launch secret token before any session, page, autoload, metadata or row reaches a client, compare it in constant time, have Stata open the tokenized 127.0.0.1 URL, and never run without a token: an app started without one makes its own and writes its link to a private file, and only if no folder takes that file prints the link once, after a warning, and keeps serving (maintainer decision M4, ratified 01oct2026; round 2, answer A).
  - Resolution: Fixed 01oct2026 (WP-29, P0.12a). Every launch of the served app has a key, and nothing is served without it. _dash_token_auth is Gate A: a Bokeh AuthProvider that refuses every page, /autoload.js, /metadata and websocket request without the key with a constant 403 before any handler runs (python app.py and dash serve). _dash_session_token_ok in make_document is Gate B: it refuses every session without the key before the rate limiter and before the data is decoded; it is the only gate under bokeh serve, where a start without DASH_SERVE_TOKEN makes its own key at the first session (_dash_process_key, _dash_bokeh_serve_key). The key is _dash_new_token (secrets, 256 bits), checked by _dash_token_valid and compared by _dash_token_matches (hmac.compare_digest); a websocket's session JWT is read by _dash_ws_payload, bounded before Bokeh decodes it. dash serve hands the key to the app with --token-stdin on S08's stdin pipe, after the app text, never in argv; _dash_write_link writes the link to a 0600 link.html in the run folder, or to a fresh private folder when the run folder cannot hold 0600, or, where no folder can, writes that file with one dash: note: naming it (ratified 01oct2026); the path is printed and the key never is; where no file can be written at all, the link is printed once after a warning line while the server keeps serving (ratified 01oct2026, round 2). A start given no key makes its own (_dash_server_app before any session under python app.py; _dash_process_key and _dash_bokeh_serve_key at the first session under bokeh serve); its link is written by _dash_announce_key through _dash_private_page, 0600 in a fresh 0700 folder, and only the path is printed. _dash_open_tokenized opens the link with no key in argv, _dash_tokenized_url names 127.0.0.1, never localhost, and the redaction (_dash_redact_query, _dash_install_access_log_redaction) keeps every query string out of Tornado's logs and the launcher's forwarded output. Pinned by test/test_serve_token.py::TestTheServedAppRequiresItsToken::test_a_session_without_the_token_reads_no_rows, test/test_serve_token.py::TestTheServedAppRequiresItsToken::test_the_page_without_the_token_is_403, test/test_serve_token.py::TestBokehServeAlwaysHasAKey::test_without_the_env_the_app_makes_a_key_and_announces_it, test/test_serve_token.py::TestTheServedAppRequiresItsToken::test_a_keyless_start_makes_a_key_and_a_private_link, test/test_serve_token.py::TestTheSessionGate::test_a_session_without_the_token_gets_only_the_refusal, test/test_serve_token.py::TestTheSessionGate::test_no_configured_token_makes_one_and_still_refuses, test/test_serve_launch.cscript TOK-02. Residual, deferred (WP-29): (1) Linux and Windows hosts are not measured (the redirect-file opener under a snap-confined browser; the stdin pipe on Windows); (2) under a hand-run python app.py each refused request logs one redacted WARNING line, with no throttle; (3) under bokeh serve only Gate B applies, so /autoload.js and /metadata answer 200 with the refusal page and no data; (4) a keyless websocket attempt may inflate up to 262,144 bytes before refusal; (5) under bokeh serve without DASH_SERVE_TOKEN the self-made link names no --prefix, waits for the first page request when the first session came over a websocket, cannot be made under --unix-socket or a port under 1024 (one line says so; every session stays refused), and its page stays blank unless the server was started with --allow-websocket-origin 127.0.0.1:<port> (the app prints that hint); (6) a link folder made for a self-made key outlives a hard kill (SIGKILL) of its process, holding a key that no longer opens anything; so does one whose hand-run python app.py is stopped by SIGTERM, which skips the app's cleanup (found in testing, WP-29 P0.12a); (7) on a disk that keeps no file permissions the link file holding the key is written anyway, readable by other accounts while the server runs, with one dash: note: naming it (ratified 01oct2026: no privacy condition is refused); (8) when no link file can be written anywhere, the link and its key are printed once, after a warning line, to the output of whoever started the server, and so into Stata's Results and any open Stata log under dash serve (batch logs are 0644), readable by whoever can read that output while the server runs (ratified 01oct2026 round 2, "Print the URL once"). Closes GAPS2 I3 (WP-29, I3).

- [x] Title: The served app, spec and data files are written with the default umask, readable by other accounts where the temp directory is shared
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py at 7421d3d: main (31888; open(output_path, "w") at 31940); dash.ado at 7421d3d: _dash_serve (7588; tempfiles at 7598 and 7652), _dash_write_data (4308)

Every temporary copy of the data -- the spec and data files of the one-line form, dash build and dash serve, and dash serve's app -- is written by dash_render.py's _dash_private_write (O_NOFOLLOW, O_NONBLOCK, created 0600, fstat-checked regular, single-link and owned, fchmod 0600 whatever the umask) into c(tmpdir)dash-<uid>/run-<pid>-<random>/ (0700; _dash_private_root notes a c(tmpdir) others can change and a folder the disk will not keep private, and leaves a linked, foreign or non-folder dash-<uid> alone for a dash-<uid>-<random> fallback made by _dash_fallback_root -- no privacy condition is refused, as ratified 01oct2026; the anti-hijack refusals end r(7102), and only a failure to create the folder at all ends r(603)), opened by dash.ado's _dash_tmp_open and removed by _dash_tmp_close, with folders left by an error or crash swept by _dash_run_sweep; the spec and empty-data files are written from Python (_dash_tmp_write_text) because Stata's file write resets the mode to the umask; dash serve's spec and data are erased once its app is written; every server app, dash build, server's user-named .py included (M4), is written 0600 by ServerAppBuilder.build(private=True), which removes an existing file of the user's at the name with _dash_private_clear_name (lstat, refusing a link, a non-regular or a foreign file) and then creates the file with O_EXCL; pages the user names keep the umask, as twoway's saving() and graph export; _dash_launch_app no longer runs `python <app>`: _dash_read_verified_app opens the app with O_NOFOLLOW and checks the open descriptor's type, owner, (st_dev, st_ino) and size and the bytes' SHA-256 against the _DashWrittenApp main() returned, and _dash_hand_over writes those bytes as one DASHAPP1 frame to the stdin of `python -P -c _DASH_BOOT <app>`, which compiles them under the app's name and runs them as __main__, so a path or folder swapped in after the check cannot change what runs and no module beside the app or in the working folder is imported (ratified 01oct2026, round 2); S08's commits add no file write to the served app (S13 later adds the hand-started app's private link.html). The saved page and the served app are both covered: the spec and data feed both renderers, the preview is the saved page, the app is the served one. - [x] Title: dash_setup fails on PEP 668 externally managed Pythons, and the commands it prints fail too
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_setup.ado: dash_setup (its venv() block, the detection before step 2, steps 2 and 3, the below verdict), _dash_pip_command, _dash_setup_summary (venvready), and the new _dash_setup_lib, _dash_setup_detect, _dash_setup_pip, _dash_setup_guide and _dash_setup_venv; dash_setup_lib.py (new: run_child, detect_environment, pip_install_argv, shell_line, add_user_site, validate_venv_path, create_venv, verify_in and the stata_* entry points); dash_setup.sthlp (Syntax, Description, Options, Externally managed Pythons, Troubleshooting); dash.sthlp (Setup syntax, Dependencies)
  - Description: DROPIN-REMAINING.md P0.19, verified at 357c368: `dash_setup` fails on externally-managed Pythons (PEP 668, e.g. Homebrew). There is no detection and no `venv()` option. The manual fallback names a bare, unquoted `python`, and the single-quoted hint breaks in cmd.exe. The `--user` site is not added to the path, there is no ensurepip hint, and the help gives no guidance. Sources: GAPS2-H7a, GAPS2-H7b, GAPS2-H7c, GAPS2-H7d, GAPS2-H7e, GAPS2-H7f, GAPS2-H7g. Measured with them (WP-29 section 09): N1, under Stata's batch locale (US-ASCII) the non-ASCII byte in pip's PEP 668 message ended dash_setup with r(7102); N2, pip ran sys.executable, the base interpreter under a Homebrew venv link, so even a venv was refused; N3, pip ran from Stata's working directory, so a pip/ package there ran in its place (security); N4, the "To upgrade" line printed on a managed Python was itself refused.
  - Suggested fix: WP-29 section 09 (dash_setup on PEP 668 Pythons): detect an externally managed Python before any pip process starts, offer venv(path), and print commands that run as printed in cmd.exe and POSIX shells.
  - Resolution: Fixed 01oct2026 (WP-29, P0.19). dash_setup inspects the linked Python in a child process (dash_setup_lib.detect_environment) and on an externally managed or pip-less Python runs no pip, printing the PEP 668 or ensurepip guidance (H7a, H7g); dash_setup, venv(path) creates or reuses, installs into and verifies a private environment and prints the python set exec line (H7b); every printed command is the resolved c(python_exec) quoted by dash_setup_lib.shell_line for POSIX shells and cmd.exe, and a managed Python gets no upgrade line (H7c, H7d, H7e, N4); a --user install is added to sys.path in the same run (H7f); pip's output is decoded as UTF-8 (N1); pip runs c(python_exec), not sys.executable (N2), from a private directory with -P, without an inherited PYTHONPATH and with PIP_BREAK_SYSTEM_PACKAGES=0 (N3, security). No renderer change; a venv-linked session builds a saved page and serves /health (scripts/release_gate_venv.do). Pinned by test/test_setup_pep668.py::TestRunChild::test_a_pip_package_in_the_working_directory_is_not_run, test/test_setup_pep668.py::TestRunChild::test_non_ascii_output_under_an_ascii_locale_is_decoded, test/test_setup_pep668.py::TestShellLine::test_the_posix_line_survives_sh, test/test_setup_pep668.py::TestValidateVenvPath::test_refusals, test/test_program_coverage.cscript PEP-01, test/test_program_coverage.cscript PEP-08, test/test_setup_honesty.cscript PEP-18; fixture test/fixtures/pip_refusals.json. Residual, deferred (WP-29): Windows quoting, Scripts\python.exe and Debian's ensurepip-less venv are tested as pure functions only; dash's own helper and in-process imports are found in the working directory first (Stata's and Python's rule). Closes GAPS2 H7 (WP-29, H7).

  - Resolution: Fixed 08oct2026 (WP-30, P1.23a). Each axis's date kind is decided by the layers drawn on it, reading the range (yvar1, yvar2) and paired (y1var, x1var, y2var, x2var) keys and skipping scatteri, pci, pcarrowi and function (_dash_figure_date_kind and _dash_axis_vars with axis_no, _dash_layer_axis_names), so a yaxis(2) or xaxis(2) layer leaves the first axis's dates, and a second axis of dates is a date axis in its variable's format whose axis(2) labels, ticks, lines, range() and #N ticks read dates (_dash_mark_date_axes, _dash_axis_date_kind for y2 and x2, _dash_add_secondary_axes, _dash_finish_secondary_axes, _dash_count_axes, _dash_refline_draw). Computed layers, bar widths and default bases follow the axis a layer is drawn on (GlyphMapper._unit_kind through _on_axis, _bar_extent and _base_zero); scatteri, pci and pcarrowi coordinates and function points are placed in date units on a date axis (GlyphMapper._literal_on_axis), and an explicit base() is read in date units (GlyphMapper._base_in_axis_units); one outside 01jan0100 to 31dec9999 is drawn at its number as twoway draws it, with no note, converted by millisecond and civil-calendar arithmetic that holds every year a browser can draw (_dash_literal_to_ms, _dash_days_from_civil), and only a value past the browser's dates (|ms| > 8.64e15) is left out with one note. An axis reaching past Stata's dates is ticked by natscale over its Stata numbers (_dash_off_date_ticks, _dash_finish_off_date_axes) and labelled with each number as display writes it (_dash_stata_number_of, dash_stata_number_of), never by Bokeh's DatetimeTicker. A raw date beside a plain number on one axis is drawn at its Stata values through one shared browser-side transform per date kind (_dash_date_transform, _dash_layer_in_axis_units), whose Python twin (_dash_spec_units with _dash_date_units) feeds _dash_secondary_values, the hull readers and the by() scale and whose JS twin feeds the saved re-finish; the axis is labelled in the first layer's date format (_dash_axis_unit_format) and xlabel(minmax) reads Stata values. Both renderers draw alike, before and after a filter move, and the transform renders under the page's security policy. Its REM-08-04 ids are confirmed by content against REMAINING.md:1935-2110. - [ ] Title: Five scheme keys are parsed and read by nothing
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py SchemeParser._init_properties (by_legend_ring, zyx2_ring, text_option_vertical, numticks_minor, legend_span); test/test_scheme_consumption.py _UNREAD_KEYS
  - Description: Found by WP-32 (BUGS.md "Harness guards") when test_the_key_is_read_somewhere took its keys from every attribute _init_properties assigns instead of a hand-written list of 22: of 140 parsed keys, six have no reader in dash_render.py. One is by design (note_font_size: Stata's note() box reads `gsize small_body`, not `gsize note`). Five are keys twoway's style files read and dash parses and then ignores, so a scheme that changes them draws no differently in dash: `gridringstyle by_legend_ring` and `gridringstyle zyx2legend_ring` (bygraphstyle-*.style's legend_ring and zyx2legend_ring), `vertical_text text_option` (textboxstyle-text_option.style), `numticks_g horizontal_minor` and `vertical_minor` (ticksetstyle-minor_*.style) and `yesno legend_span` (bygraphstyle-*.style's legend_span). Every shipped scheme gives the values dash draws by default (s2color and stcolor: ring 3 and 4, middle, 0 minor ticks, no span), so only a user's scheme shows the difference.
  - Suggested fix: give each key its consumer in the shared drawing code (both modes), measured against twoway with a user scheme that changes it, and take it off _UNREAD_KEYS.
  - Resolution: Not fixed: it stays open because each key needs its own consumer in both renderers and a twoway measurement with a user scheme, which is drawing work beyond the harness guard that found them. Pinned by test/test_scheme_consumption.py::TestNoParsedKeyIsDiscarded::test_an_unread_key_is_still_unread, which fails the day a key gains a reader. Graded S3 (WP-32): no shipped scheme draws differently; a user scheme's value for these keys is ignored.

- [x] Title: No secret scan, CI, ruff, pyflakes or bandit, the hooks CLAUDE.md relies on are git-ignored, and *.log is excluded only locally
  - File Names and Line Numbers: Makefile:24-92; .gitignore; .git/info/exclude:130
  - Description: GAPS3.md I6, re-verified at 6370ca4: No secret scan; no CI; no ruff/pyflakes/bandit in the Makefile (the renderer has 51 findings); `.claude/hooks/*` that CLAUDE.md relies on are git-ignored; `*.log` excluded only locally so a fresh clone shows test/run_all_cscripts.log as untracked.

  - Resolution: Fixed 18oct2026 (WP-31, I6). `make lint` runs ruff (pyflakes' F rules and pycodestyle's E4/E7/E9, ruff's default set) over dash_render.py, dash_setup_lib.py, test/ and scripts/ with the committed ruff.toml; it names RUFF, else `python -m ruff`, else ruff on PATH, and when none is installed says how to install it and exits 2 (ruff is not a dependency). The baseline is greppable: 40 `# noqa: <code>  # <why>` comments in dash_render.py (17 unused imports kept, 12 string annotations, 6 unused locals, 4 repeated scheme-default keys whose later entry is in force, 1 dtype comparison; no code changed) and per-file ignores for test/ and scripts/ (unused and joined imports, fixture shadowing, unused locals). E, W and B in full report about 3,800 style findings (E501 2,648), so the default set was chosen; bandit is not added (the secrets scan covers the leak class it would). test/test_no_secrets.py scans every tracked file for AWS, PEM, GitHub, Slack and DASH_SERVE_TOKEN key shapes (the suite's published TEST_TOKEN allowed) and the maintainer's address (from git config, allowed only in .ultraplan/). .github/workflows/test.yml runs `make test-dev` (DEV_STRICT=0 DEV_BASELINE=py311, new make variables whose defaults keep make test-dev strict on dev) and `make lint` on ubuntu-latest under Python 3.11 with no Stata step and no secret; it names macOS as the certified platform. .gitignore carries *.log. The .claude/hooks scripts stay untracked (they hold machine paths); CLAUDE.md rules 9-10 name them and README's Development section gets the line documenting them (S59 owns README). Pinned by test/test_no_secrets.py, test/test_repo_hygiene.py and test/test_cert_verdict.py::TestMakeCheckIsWired::test_test_dev_is_strict_under_the_development_interpreter. Closes GAPS3 I6 (WP-31, I6).

  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado _dash_label_split, the plot parser's lalpha() declaration
  - Description: GAPS3.md C17, found by WP-31 section 34 (unfiled): twoway takes `lal(center)` as lalign() with rc 0; dash maps lal() .. lalpha() to its own lalpha() (an option twoway does not have), so `lal(center)` is refused or misread.

Measured first (scripts/extract_colour_width_edges_truth.do, lal.*, with outside because inside is a line's default): twoway reads la(), lal(), lali(), lalig() and lalign() as lalign() (the line's align setting outside), reads l() as l1title() (the setting stays inside; test_abbreviations.cscript U27-11), and refuses lalp() and lalpha(), "option lalp() not allowed", r(198). dash read lal() as its own lalpha() and refused lal(outside), "must be a number". dash.ado's plot parser now declares LALPha(), so lalpha() starts at lalp, and _dash_label_split reads every lal() as lalign() (its forced lal()-to-lalpha() branch is gone); lalign()'s minimum stays la, as twoway's.   - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py SchemeParser._init_properties (the font-size reads before the size_ref_in block), SchemeParser._gsize
  - Description: GAPS3.md E11, found by WP-31 section 32 (E11): _init_properties reads every gsize (heading, axis_title, tick_label, note, ...) through _gsize, which converts a #pt value at 4 / size_ref_in, before it sets size_ref_in to min(graphsize x, graphsize y); the first read finds no size_ref_in and uses 4.0.   - Suggested fix: WP-31 section 44 (style file resolver): set size_ref_in from the scheme's graphsize before the first _gsize read (read graphsize first), measured against twoway with such a user scheme.
  - Resolution: Fixed 16oct2026 (WP-31, E11b). `SchemeParser._init_properties` sets `size_ref_in` from the scheme's graphsize x/y (the smaller side) before the gsize block reads `_gsize`, so a #-pt gsize converts at the scheme's own reference: measured, `gsize heading 12-pt` under a 3.12 x 2.392 in scheme is 12 points on the graph, 20.067pt in dash's 4-inch units; both renderers share SchemeParser. The pool is now _dash_minor_pool_size's: for a #N axis the bound of twoway's rule over any scale the axis can take -- at most N + 1 majors (natscale's largest answer), ##N's positions an interval, four intervals more, the span widened by the axis's margin either side (held over 20,000 random ranges) -- S35's size as the floor and the tick cap as the ceiling, in both renderers.   - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_parse.mata:1594 (_dash_colorrule_check), :1647 (_dash_colorrule_full); dash.ado:2599 (_dash_contour_check), :2736 (_dash_fold_typed)
