- [x] Title: mcolor(255 0,0) is refused where twoway notes the named style and draws
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash.ado _dash_subopt_colour_check / _dash_stylelist_check (the comma-colour refusal)
  - Description: Found by the 18oct2026 follow-up to WP-31 section 56. twoway takes `mcolor(255 0,0)` with rc 0 and its "named style 255 not found" note; dash refuses it r(198) "invalid '0'", the refusal twoway gives `mcolor(255,0,0)` (which dash matches).
  - Suggested fix: refuse a comma colour only when twoway does (measure which blank-and-comma forms twoway reads as a named style), and note the rest in twoway's words.
  - Resolution: Fixed 18oct2026. Measured (StataNow 19.5, s2color, fourteen blank-and-comma forms on mcolor() with one and two y, lcolor(), fcolor(), mlabcolor() and the thirteen structured sub-options of WP-31 E5, SVG export for the drawn ones): twoway reads a colour and its own " editcopy" as parts between commas, every second of which must be blank -- the first that is not is "invalid '<its first word>'", r(198) (255,0,0 '0', red, 'editcopy', 1,,2,3 '3', red,"blue" '"blue') -- and draws the rest as its other parts joined by blanks (1,,2 is "1 2", noted, black; 255,,0,,0 red; red*2,,blue the default, as red*2 blue); on a plot option this holds for each stylelist element a y uses, so mcolor(255 0,0) on one y is the element 255, noted and drawn black, and on two y "invalid '0'"; a sub-option's value is read whole. dash read the whole plot value and refused at its first comma. Now _dash_colour_comma (Mata, new) gives twoway's word: the colour kind applies it to each used element from _dash_stylelist_check (_dash_validate_opts no longer reads the whole value), _dash_subopt_colour_comma to the sub-option's value, quotes inside it counted as text; _dash_stylelist_elems keeps the text glued after a quoted element as the next element, so mcolor("red",blue) on two y is "invalid 'blue'" as in twoway. The renderer reads a form twoway takes as its blank form (OptionTranslator._colour_commas, both renderers) and names an unknown colour whole, its *# and %# left off, as twoway names it (mcolor("300 0 0") "named style 300 0 0"; dash.ado still hands mcolor(300 0 0) over as its element 300). The help's validation and Colours paragraphs say so. Pinned by test/test_option_validation.cscript CG-09 (252 forms and hosts, rc and refusal line against twoway's, live) and test/test_colour_grammar.py::TestBothModes::test_a_comma_colour_twoway_draws_is_its_blank_form, ::test_the_note_names_what_twoway_names, ::TestTheParts::test_the_commas_twoway_draws.

- [x] Title: A quote inside a compound-quoted mlabfontface() value gives r(198) where twoway gives r(132)
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_parse.mata _dash_mlabff_refusal
  - Description: Found by the 18oct2026 follow-up to WP-31 section 56. `mlabfontface(`"a"b"')` is r(132) in twoway; dash refuses it r(198). Every other measured mlabfontface() form matches (test_abbreviations.cscript MLF-01).
  - Suggested fix: give twoway's r(132) and words for a quote inside a compound-quoted value.
  - Resolution: Fixed 18oct2026. Measured (StataNow 19.5): a compound-quoted mlabfontface() value is read to the compound quote that closes it, nested ones kept (mlabfontface(`"a`"b"'c"') is the one-word refusal of a`"b"'c); a double quote inside it, with no blank before the first, is r(132) when the count of them is odd, twoway's line broken where its own display of the value broke ("option(s) fontface(`too many ')' or ']'", the text between a leading quote and the next before "too many": `""a"' gives "fontface(`atoo many"), and the one-word refusal when it is even, a leading "..." losing its quotes (`""ab"c"' is fontface(`abc"'), `""""' the empty form); a blank before the first quote keeps the r(111) "not found" refusal. _dash_mlabff_refusal reads it so. Pinned by test/test_abbreviations.cscript MLF-01 (13 more quoted values, rc and first error line against twoway's).

- [ ] Title: dash_setup installs by version, not by hash
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_setup.ado (_dash_setup_pip); dash_setup_lib.py pip_install_argv
  - Description: Residual of GAPS3 I3 (WP-31 section 59): dash_setup installs packaging, bokeh, numpy and pandas from the index by version range (pip install "bokeh>=3.8,<3.10"), never with --require-hashes; a hash-pinned install needs every transitive wheel's hash for each platform and Python, which only a maintained lock file can hold.
  - Suggested fix: ship a lock file of hashes per supported platform and Python, regenerated at each release, and install with --require-hashes from it (ratification item 1 of WP-31 section 59).
  - Resolution: Not fixed: deferred at WP-31's closeout because hash pinning needs a maintained per-platform lock file (DECISIONS D38: hash-pinned installs stay deferred; WP-31 section 59, ratification item 1). Graded S3 (WP-31): supply-chain hardening of an install the user runs.

- [x] Title: A quoted colour inside a title, line or label sub-option is drawn black with its quotes named
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py OptionTranslator.stata_colour, OptionTranslator.parse_color_alpha
  - Description: Found by the 18oct2026 follow-up to WP-31 section 56 (test/fixtures/colour_width_edges_truth.json sp.title.color). twoway draws title("T", color("1 2 3")), its compound-quoted form, xline(3000, lcolor("1 2 3")), ylabel(, labcolor("1 2 3")), legend(color("1 2 3")) and note("T", color("1 2 3")) #010203, and notes color("1,,2") as "named style 1 2" and color("bogus") as "named style bogus" (measured 18oct2026, SVG export). dash's renderer received those values with their quotes (the region options' reader already removed them), drew them black and noted the quoted text, "named style "1 2 3"".
  - Suggested fix: read an option's colour without one enclosing pair of quotes, in both renderers.
  - Resolution: Fixed 18oct2026. OptionTranslator._colour_unquote (new) removes one enclosing plain or compound pair from an option's colour before stata_colour reads it and before the note names it; a quote with no partner is kept (plotregion(color("255 0 0)) is still black, named "255 0 0 with its quote). The same measurement found mcolor(red,"blue") "invalid '"blue'", r(198), on one y and two, which dash already gives (test/test_option_validation.cscript CG-09). Pinned by test/test_colour_grammar.py::TestBothModes::test_a_quoted_sub_option_colour_is_its_text and ::TestTheParts::test_one_enclosing_quote_pair_is_removed.

- [x] Title: The axe example-page run fails on two pages when its workers fetch axe-core at once
  - File Names and Line Numbers: test/axe_fetch.py axe_source
  - Description: Found by WP-31's closeout gate, 18oct2026: `DASH_STRICT=1 DASH_TEST_TIER=release python3 -m pytest test/test_accessibility_axe.py -k examples` over the 14 example pages `make gate` built gave 12 passed and 2 errors, FileNotFoundError renaming `<tmp>/dash_axe_4.12.1/axe.min.js.part` to `axe.min.js`: every xdist worker's module fixture fetched axe-core into the one folder through the one part-file name, and a worker whose part file another had already renamed failed.
  - Suggested fix: write each fetch to a part file of its own before the rename.
  - Resolution: Fixed 18oct2026. axe_source writes through tempfile.mkstemp in the folder (removed if the write or rename fails) and renames it over axe.min.js; the rerun gave 14 passed, 0 violations. Pinned by test/test_axe_fetch.py::test_concurrent_fetches_each_write_their_own_part_file (four fetches that all reach their rename before any runs; red before the fix).

- [x] Title: A legend of marker keys grows its key box to 2.5 times the marker instead of twoway's key size
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py _dash_apply_legend (3b. the key geometry)
  - Description: Maintainer ruling D39 (D-31.a), 18oct2026. _dash_apply_legend raised a key box holding a marker to ceil(size / 0.4) px, and a legend of marker keys only took that as its width, so Bokeh (which draws a legend marker at 0.4 of the box) drew the key marker at the plot's size: `scatter mpg weight || scatter price weight` drew 15 x 15 px keys under s2color, and msize(huge) widened the legend. twoway's key size is symxsize() by symysize() (legend_geometry_truth.json default_geometry: key_xsize 13, key_ysize 3.4722 on the two-scatter legend).
  - Suggested fix: give every key box symxsize() by symysize(), as on a line legend.
  - Resolution: Fixed 18oct2026 (WP-32, D-31.a). The marker-size growth is removed: every legend key box is the scheme's legend_key_xsize by legend_key_ysize, or symxsize() by symysize(), 50 x 13 px under s2color, so forcesize and noforcesize draw the same box. The browser draws a key's marker at 0.4 of the box's smaller side (5.2 px), twoway at the marker's own size with a key only as wide as the marker; documented in the help. Pinned by test/test_legend_geometry.py::TestDefaultGeometry::test_a_marker_key_takes_twoways_key_size, test/test_legend_geometry.py::TestDefaultGeometry::test_a_large_marker_does_not_grow_the_key; fixture test/fixtures/legend_geometry_truth.json.

- [x] Title: A framed title, subtitle, note or caption box has no margin round its text
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py _dash_textbox_style (box); dash-*.scheme
  - Description: Maintainer ruling D39 (D-30.c), 18oct2026. Section 30 held an unspanned box narrower than dash's; measured 18oct2026 (StataNow 19.5, s2color and stcolor, SVG): twoway sizes every box, spanned or not, to its text plus its text box style's margin (title("Hello world", box justification(left)), subtitle, note and caption start their text 0.6 units inside the box, s2color's `margin heading/subheading/body/small_body vsmall`), and span only centres the box on the graph instead of the plot region. Bokeh draws a Title's box round its text and padding, and dash gave no padding without margin(), so the box hugged the text.
  - Suggested fix: pad a framed text box by its text box style's margin.
  - Resolution: Fixed 18oct2026 (WP-32, D-30.c). _dash_textbox_margin_px (new) reads the text box style (tstyle(), else the scheme's `textboxstyle <option>`) and its `margin <name>` through the scheme's margin ladder, and _dash_textbox_style pads a framed box by it when margin() is not given, in both renderers. scripts/extract_scheme_truth.py carries the six directives (textboxstyle title, subtitle, caption; margin heading, body, small_body) into every dash-*.scheme and test/fixtures/scheme_truth.json. span still keeps the box centred on the plot region, documented in the help. Pinned by test/test_textbox_placement.py::TestBox::test_an_unspanned_box_is_its_text_and_margin, test/test_textbox_placement.py::TestBox::test_no_box_keeps_no_padding; fixture test/fixtures/scheme_truth.json.

- [x] Title: colorvar() on a line plot draws the whole line in its first point's level
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py GlyphMapper.map_line, GlyphMapper.map_rline, GlyphMapper._colorvar_paint
  - Description: Maintainer ruling D39 (D-15f), 18oct2026. A Bokeh Line takes one colour, so section 15 drew a line, tsline, rline's bounds and connected's and rconnected's lines in the colour of the first finite row's level. Measured 18oct2026 (StataNow 19.5, s2color and stcolor, SVG; colordiscrete and continuous, connect(stairstep), connected): twoway draws one path a colour level through that level's points in plot order -- on x 1..6 with z 1 1 2 2 1 3 the paths x 1 2 5 and x 3 4, level 3's one point nothing -- and the rows missing z one path in the colormissing() colour, drawn first; it colours no segment between two levels.
  - Suggested fix: draw one line a level, each from its level's rows.
  - Resolution: Fixed 18oct2026 (WP-32, D-15f). GlyphMapper._colorvar_line_parts (new) builds the colour key through _apply_colorvar and splits the line's rows by GlyphMapper._colorvar_level_index (new, BokehJS's binning, vectorised) into one source a level -- the missing level first, then every level of the layer's colour rows, empty ones too, so the served redraw pairs them by position -- and GlyphMapper._colorvar_line_draw (new) draws each by connect() and cmissing() in its level's colour, in map_line (line, tsline, connected, rconnected) and map_rline (rline, tsrline). Each source carries the row ids, so the saved page's filter callback keeps a level's rows after a move; the served app redraws them. Pinned by test/test_colorvar_line_levels.py::TestOneLinePerLevel::test_the_measured_paths, test/test_colorvar_line_levels.py::TestOneLinePerLevel::test_missing_levels_are_one_grey_line, test/test_colorvar_line_levels.py::TestOneLinePerLevel::test_each_bound_is_one_line_a_level, test/test_colorvar_line_levels.py::TestAfterAMove::test_saved, test/test_colorvar_line_levels.py::TestAfterAMove::test_served.

- [x] Title: graphregion(margin()) stays at the pixels of the size the page was built at
  - File Names and Line Numbers: dash_render.py _dash_graph_margin, _dash_by_array_styles
  - Description: Maintainer ruling D39 (D-37.a), 18oct2026. _dash_graph_margin added the margin's change times min(fig.width, fig.height) to the figure's min_border_* once, at build, and a page resized to another width kept those pixels; _dash_by_array_styles inset a by() array by fixed px at dash's 4-inch reference (3.84 px a unit). twoway's margin is a share of the graph's smaller side at any size (WP-31 D11's measurement), and measured 18oct2026 (StataNow 19.5, stcolor, SVG) by(foreign, graphregion(margin(l+20 t+10))) insets the whole array by 20 and 10 units while graphregion(margin(l+20 t+10)) outside by() draws exactly the graph without it.
  - Suggested fix: re-derive the borders from the drawn size on a resize, and give the by() inset in a unit that scales with the graph.
  - Resolution: Fixed 18oct2026 (WP-32, D-37.a). _dash_graph_margin attaches one CustomJS (_DASH_GRAPH_MARGIN_JS, new) on the figure's outer_width and outer_height that replaces each changed side's added px with the change times min(W, H) / 100, keeping what other passes added to the border; _dash_by_array_styles writes the array's padding as a CSS percentage of the cell's width, the units times min(W, H) / W from xsize()/ysize() or the scheme's graphsize (_dash_short_side_share, new), so the inset scales with the page; both renderers. A graphregion(margin()) outside by() on a by() graph still draws nothing, as in twoway. Pinned by test/test_region_remainder.py::TestGraphMargin::test_a_resize_redraws_the_margin, test/test_by_array.py::TestArrayInset::test_graph_margin, test/test_by_array.py::TestArrayInset::test_the_inset_follows_the_graphs_ratio.
